title: Rhea Lend (ex-Burrow) margin-trading exploit on NEAR
summary: On 16 Apr 2026 an attacker used fake NEP-141 tokens and purpose-built Ref pools to pass Burrowland's margin slippage check, which summed intermediate route minimums. Over about 80 minutes (08:22-09:42 UTC per QuillAudits) they opened margin positions that drained ~$18.4M of real USDC, USDT, wNEAR and ZEC from contract.main.burrow.near. The ledger utilization the UI shows fell during the drain, while the contract's actual token balances collapsed: USDC 6.88M to 0.44M, wNEAR 2.45M to 3k. Guardian sunhao.near disabled every asset on-chain from 09:54:23 to 10:06. The first public alert (CertiK) came at 14:55 and Rhea's first post at 17:33. The contract was upgraded into Maintenance mode on 28 Apr and reopened to users on 12 May 15:40, with balances reconciled and Rhea covering the residual deficit.

positions_considered.description: Supplies native USDC (~$1,000) on Rhea Lend, no debt
wNEAR collateral, native USDC debt, health factor about 1.6

t_incident_start.description: First exploit tx per QuillAudits (08:22-09:42, 1,142 txs). A USDC reserve dip during a margin settlement began at 08:09:25 and is possibly related.

t_first_public_signal.description: First on-chain reading where USDC/USDT token balances held by contract.main.burrow.near diverge sharply from the ledger's available liquidity (USDC 5.12M vs 7.09M). Only a monitor that compares ft_balance_of with the ledger would see it; utilization fell. The first off-chain public signal was CertiK at 14:55:14.

t_point_of_no_return.definition: Guardian disables the asset on-chain (can_withdraw=false): wNEAR 09:54:23, USDT 09:54:39, USDC 09:54:46. After that neither archetype can withdraw or repay-and-withdraw until 12 May. For large holders the effective PONR came earlier: USDC held fell to 0.44M by 09:10 and wNEAR held to 8.5k by 09:35.

t_protocol_first_ack.description: First Rhea X post ('temporarily paused the contracts'). Earlier protocol actions: on-chain guardian freeze at 09:54:23 (no text), DAO proposal 1492 'Unregister margin dex' at 14:08:15, and DAO proposal 1494 'Transfer messsage to hacker' at 16:56:45.

lead_time_minutes.notes: On-chain balance-vs-ledger signal at 08:45:00 came 69 min before the 09:54:23 freeze. If the first signal is taken from off-chain sources (CertiK 14:55:14), the lead time is -301 min (5 h after the freeze). Rhea's first X post (17:33) was -459 min. With the 08:09:25 reserve dip as start, start-to-PONR is 105 min.

outcome_passive_holder.outcome: Withdrawals worked until 09:54:46 for small amounts; the contract never held less than ~0.44M USDC before the freeze. Then frozen. Ledger balances were reconciled (USDC supplied 26.85M at reopening vs 26.95M before the exploit; Rhea: 'All 100% of user balances accounted for'; QuillAudits: remaining ~$0.4M deficit covered by Rhea). Users could withdraw again from 12 May 15:39 UTC. On reopening, USDC utilization rose from 76% to 87%, with ~1.5M liquidity left.
outcome_passive_holder.loss_estimate: No principal loss reported. Ledger interest kept accruing during the freeze (USDC borrowed 20.450M on 16 Apr, 20.510M on 25 Apr). Balances were flat in Maintenance mode (29 Apr-12 May). Whether the freeze-period interest survived reconciliation is unclear; at worst ~26 days of yield were lost.

outcome_passive_holder.outcome: Could repay and withdraw wNEAR until 09:54:23 if collateral was below the contract's shrinking wNEAR balance (8.5k NEAR by 09:35). Then frozen. NEAR moved only -2% that day, so health factor was unaffected. Debt and collateral preserved; the contract reopened with public liquidations disabled.
outcome_passive_holder.loss_estimate: None known. No liquidation, no reported haircut, and wNEAR interest was set to 0 by DAO proposal 1499 (19 Apr).

ground_truth.outcome_price_only_rule: No trigger. NEAR/USDT was 1.432 at 08:00 and 1.405 at 10:00 (Binance 1h), about -2%, and USDC stayed at peg. Health factors were unchanged. A utilization trigger also stays silent because ledger utilization fell (USDC 74.8% to 67.6%) while the real token balance was drained. Only a rule comparing ft_balance_of with ledger-available liquidity would have fired, from 08:40-08:45.

ideal_action.rationale: A small supplier who withdrew between 08:45 and 09:54 got out in full. Large suppliers needed to act before about 09:00, when held USDC fell below 1M.
Repaying USDC and withdrawing wNEAR needed the contract's wNEAR balance, which fell from 2.44M to 0.15M by 09:30 and to 8.5k by 09:35. A small position could exit until 09:54:23.

expected_judge_labels.rationale: Normal state; the 08:09 reserve dip is too small to act on.
Contract's real USDC is draining while its ledger shows more liquidity. Insolvency in progress.
Withdrawals disabled; no action possible. Exit when it reopens.
Reopened after an exploit, the contract was upgraded, and a withdrawal queue is forming (utilization 76% to 87%). Taking some liquidity off is reasonable.
Repay and withdraw collateral while the contract still holds wNEAR (drained 08:55-09:35).
Frozen; nothing can be done. Price risk is low because NEAR is flat.
Reopened with public liquidations disabled; reduce exposure to a freshly upgraded contract.

items.author: QuillAudits post-mortem (describing NEAR on-chain activity)
items.verbatim_text: On April 15 at 22:08–22:49 UTC, the attacker coordinated a campaign to finalise the infrastructure. Twenty-one intermediary accounts were deleted within 30 seconds at 22:48–22:49 UTC, all designating the subject wallet as sole beneficiary, covering their tracks before the main event.
items.replay_text: NEAR chain: 21 implicit accounts deleted within 30 s (22:48–22:49 UTC), all naming the same beneficiary implicit account (created 15 Apr 07:12 UTC, funded via intents.near). None of these accounts interacted with contract.main.burrow.near in this window.
items.notes: Time from QuillAudits; we did not verify the deletions on-chain. A Burrow-focused monitor would not have flagged this; included as context.

items.verbatim_text: The exploit itself ran on April 16 from 08:22 to 09:42 UTC. The attacker opened a large number of margin trading positions on Burrow Protocol using the fake token swap router.

data_gaps: First and last exploit tx hashes not pinned on-chain; we use QuillAudits' 08:22-09:42 UTC. NearBlocks rate limits stopped a full scan of contract.main.burrow.near.

Exact time of the CertiK alert is known (14:55:14 from the snowflake); no earlier PeckShield, Cyvers or other security-firm post was found. Independent researchers in an ETH Security Telegram group reportedly discussed it earlier (rekt), with no timestamp; Telegram is not allowlisted.
Rhea's own incident report and the 8 May reopening notice are X Articles; only preview text is retrievable.
No Rhea or NEAR governance forum (gov.near.org) thread about the incident was found. Burrow governance runs through on-chain Sputnik DAO proposals, which we used instead.
Whether the 08:09:25 reserve change (account cfc618ac…) was part of the exploit is not verified.

Final per-user compensation mechanics are not public. We infer restoration from the on-chain reconciliation (USDC supplied back to ~26.85M), Rhea's '100% of user balances accounted for', and QuillAudits ('remaining deficit of ~$0.4M' covered by Rhea).
The Block article page is blocked for curl; its time and quotes come from WebFetch.
Whether interest that accrued on the ledger during the freeze (16-28 Apr) was kept through the 29-30 Apr reconciliation was not determined per account.
source_quality: Strong on-chain coverage. 5-min archival-RPC readings of ledger and real token balances (08:00-10:30), exact guardian freeze, upgrade and reopen txs, and Sputnik DAO proposal times are all primary. X posts are primary through snowflake IDs and syndication text, though long posts are truncated. Exploit start and end times are secondhand (QuillAudits, minute precision). Loss figures conflict: CertiK $7.6M, QuillAudits $18.6M, Rhea/The Block $18.4M. Tether's frozen amount also varies: 3.29M in-wallet, plus 1.05M frozen in Intents.
